text:
sqlpipe moves Postgres tables into S3 as Parquet through three stages joined by bounded channels.

**Reader** holds a single Postgres connection, runs a cursor over target table, pulls rows in fixed-size batches. Batch size caps memory: reader blocks when downstream channel full, so slow S3 backpressures straight to database instead of buffering unbounded.

**Converter** takes each batch, maps Postgres types to Parquet schema once at start, writes rows into a row group, closes group at batch boundary. Output is byte buffer per row group. CPU-bound stage, so it scales horizontally — several converters read same channel, order irrelevant because row groups are self-contained.

**Uploader** accumulates row-group buffers until it hits S3 multipart minimum (5 MiB), then uploads part. Failed part retries with exponential backoff; part numbers stay stable across retries, so retry never corrupts object. On final batch, uploader completes multipart upload; on unrecoverable error, aborts it so S3 drops orphaned parts.

Failure in any stage cancels shared context, draining the other two.
